To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the best performing algorithm for the News dataset was the one based on the combination of the cosine similarity and the TF-IDF; 2) for the Blogs dataset, the algorithm with better performance was the one that uses the cosine similarity; and 3) for the Article dataset, the best performing algorithm was the one that combines the TF-IDF and the cosine similarity.
1) The most efficient sentence scoring algorithm is LexRank, with an average of 2.2 points higher than the second best one.

(1) the best performing algorithms for extractive summarization in our experiments are: the algorithm based on the cosine similarity, the algorithm based on a combination of the cosine similarity and the term frequency, the algorithm based in the cosine similarity and a term frequency, the TF-IDF algorithm, the algorithm based only on the cosine similarity and, in the last place, the algorithm based solely on the term frequency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of 15 sentence scoring algorithms for extractive text summaries in the context of three different datasets (news, blogs and articles).
the evaluation of the performance of sentence scoring algorithms for extractive summarization in the context of three different datasets.
the assessment of the performance of sentence scoring techniques for text summarization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sentence extraction results are not very good, but there is a clear tendency for the best results.
, for the datasets and contexts used, the algorithms based on the combination of the TF-IDF and the cosine similarity, as well as the algorithms based on TF-IDF, have the best overall performance.

the best scoring techniques for extractivesummarization are: 1) the sentence scoring technique based on the use of the TF-IDF measure and the sentence length; 2) a technique that combines the TF-IDF and the sentence length with a measure of semantic similarity based on the cosine similarity of the sentence vectors; and 3) a technique based on the TF-IDF, the sentence length and the sentence location.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best sentence scoring algorithms for text summarization are those based on the TF-IDF measure.
the best sentence scoring techniques for text summarization depend on the type of text being summarized.
the best results for the three different datasets were obtained with the algorithm that uses the cosine similarity and the TF-IDF weighting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is not a sentence scoring technique that can be applied for any context.
the sentence scoring technique is not a trivial task and that the results obtained by the sentence scoring algorithms are not consistent across datasets.

sentence scoring techniques can be used in the extractive summarization process to obtain good results, but it is necessary to evaluate each technique in the specific context to obtain the best results.
